questions.stem: The stem-and-leaf diagram shows the test marks of 15 students.$$\begin{array}{r|l} 3 & 2 \;\; 5 \;\; 8 \\ 4 & 1 \;\; 1 \;\; 4 \;\; 7 \;\; 9 \\ 5 & 0 \;\; 3 \;\; 6 \;\; 6 \;\; 6 \\ 6 & 2 \;\; 4 \end{array}$$Key: $3 \mid 2$ represents 32 marks

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: One of these students is chosen at random. Find the probability that their mark was more than 50.

questions.stem: The table shows the number of hours six students spent revising and their test scores.$$\begin{array}{l|cccccc} \text{Hours} & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6 \\ \hline \text{Score} & 42 & 50 & 55 & 63 & 70 & 74 \end{array}$$

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: What type of correlation does the data show?

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Estimate the score of a student who revised for 3.5 hours.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A teacher uses the data to estimate the score of a student who revised for 20 hours. Explain why this estimate may not be reliable.
parts.answer: 20 hours is far outside the range of the data (extrapolation)

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write down the midpoints of the four class intervals, which are used to draw a frequency polygon.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write down the coordinates of the highest point of the frequency polygon.
